---
title: "Course scheduling and TimeEdit"
---

## Trigger: scheduling email

The process starts when the scheduling team asks you to submit your availability. The personalized TimeEdit invitation typically has the subject **“You have been requested to fill out a form”**. The accompanying email explains which programme and teaching period the survey covers, what information is needed, and the submission deadline.

Use the personal link in that invitation to open your form. Do not share or publish the link. If you have questions, contact the scheduling team using the details in the email or form guide (the guide lists [planning@fs.de](mailto:planning@fs.de)).

::: {.checklist title="Checklist: complete the TimeEdit form"}

1. **Check the request details.** Read the email and form description. Note the programme, teaching period, deadline, and any programme-specific questions.
2. **Review your calendar and commitments.** Identify personal obligations and planned vacation during the teaching period before entering availability. Submit official vacation requests separately through [Veda](/management/vacation.html#1-take-vacation), and follow the [vacation communication guidance](/management/vacation.html#3-communication-notification-to-colleagues).
3. **Complete the start page.** Confirm that the lecturer is correctly preselected and leave the preselected study programme unchanged. Answer all required questions and provide any preferences or constraints the form asks for.
4. **Enter availability in the calendar.** Add your general availability during the teaching period to give the scheduling team flexibility. Availability indicates when you can teach; do not mark times as available if you have a conflicting commitment. Use recurring weeks for your regular pattern and individual weeks to adjust specific dates, such as vacation. Check which mode is selected before removing an entry: removing a recurring entry affects all selected weeks, while removing an individual-week entry affects that date.
5. **Include course-specific constraints.** Use the form questions or the scheduling email to make constraints clear if they cannot be represented by unavailable times. For **Introduction to Programming (ITP), each group should have no more than four hours of teaching per day**.
6. **Review and submit.** Check that all answers and dates are correct and required questions are complete. You can save and return later, but saving does not submit the form. Submit it by the deadline. If the calendar generates a list of entries below it, use the calendar to make changes and review your answers before submitting.
7. **Check the proposed timetable.** When it arrives, look for conflicts with other teaching and personal commitments, and verify the ITP daily limit for each group. Follow up with the scheduling team or colleagues to resolve conflicts. Ensure the module coordinator has listed the correct instructor so timetable invitations reach the right person.

:::
